subject.title: fix(tts): validate maxLength is a positive finite number

question: Should the exported `setTtsMaxLength` API become a fail-closed public writer, and if so should its supported range match the existing `/tts limit` contract of 100–4096 rather than only positive finite numbers?
rationale: The current command has an established 100–4096 product range, while the exported writer has a wider numeric signature; selecting a new external failure contract is an API and compatibility decision rather than a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Define and align the writer contract
options.body: Document and test one supported range, update the public writer and callers consistently, and provide upgrade-safe proof.

options.title: Keep validation at the command boundary
options.body: Leave the exported writer behavior unchanged and rely on the existing command-specific 100–4096 validation until an external API contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Define and align the writer contract
recommendation.body: Document and test one supported range, update the public writer and callers consistently, and provide upgrade-safe proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The verified history trail was unavailable in the read-only execution environment, so the speech-core owner should be identified from git history before deciding the public contract.
